athlete_profile.description: Where the athlete says they are and what language they read, or null when they have stated neither. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates. timezone above is the zone this build actually answered in, which may be a per-request override or the default standing in for an unstated profile; this is the separate fact of what the athlete themselves stated, and null is what tells a coach to ask.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, or null when the athlete stated only a language.

language.description: The language this athlete's prescriptions are written in, or null when they stated only a timezone.

measurement_protocol.description: The measurement this cycle declared for its own outcome, verbatim from PlanState. Progress is judged against this and not against completion; when it has not been run, progress is unproven and no wearable reading substitutes for it.

measurement.description: The runnable half of the protocol above, verbatim from PlanState, or null when this cycle declared none (issues #13, #75). It names the ordinary session this cycle measures against, the week that repeats it, and what to hold constant -- and nothing about the result. Null is a real answer: a cycle with no scheduled measurement is reported as that, not as progress being unproven for the twenty-eighth day running. Whether either reading is in yet is an observation and lives in measurement_evidence.

review_frame.description: The calendar coordinates a review is framed on. The athlete's week is Monday to Sunday; every other window in this context is a rolling span ending at as_of, so a review framed on those would answer about the last seven days rather than about the week they trained. Dates only -- nothing here judges the training in them.

cycle_day.description: 1-based day of the declared cycle at as_of, uncapped: a value past the cycle length says the declared window has run out, which is when the measurement protocol comes due. Null before the cycle opens.

detail_horizon_start.description: The earliest day this context reports session by session: the earliest of previous_week_start, cycle_start and the plan's own week start. recent_actuals and reported_activities both hold rows from here onward and no earlier -- the provider was still read over its full window, and what that window holds is reported by baseline_evidence per claim and by training_history per month. Stated so "nothing since" is read against the date nobody looked past (issue #233).

unavailable_days.description: Weekdays the athlete stated they cannot train. A separate statement, not the complement of available_days: naming a lost day confirms nothing about the others.

availability_source.description: Who stated the availability above: this turn's request, the athlete's stored evidence, or neither.

week_constraints.description: What the athlete said about THIS week that names no weekday — travelling, a hotel gym, a work week that will run late — verbatim and in the order they said it. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates; an empty array is the ordinary case and means none was stated, never that none was read. Scoped to the week and gone when it ends, which is what separates it from a standing training_preference: this constrains the plan, that one does not.

baseline_evidence.description: Each athlete_baseline field's claim beside recent evidence already in this context, with how many observations back it -- so 'once' and 'four weeks running' are distinguishable without re-deriving them. One row per scalar field, one row per strength movement, through the same row shape. Carries no verdict: no stale flag, no confidence score, no suggested value; which side is right is coaching judgment. observed is null when the window holds nothing for the field; a null window on a strength row means no strength source was read at all.

recent_actuals.description: Every session the provider holds from review_frame.detail_horizon_start onward, one row each, with the planned session it was matched to when it was matched. The provider is read over a longer window than this: matching, the cycle record and baseline_evidence all run against six weeks, and baseline_evidence states that span per claim. What starts at the horizon is what is reported session by session, because that is where a review starts reading. Older provider evidence is in training_history by month. A row whose settled attachment put its reading on a cycle_sessions record is reduced to its reconciliation identity; read the attached record's activity for its measurements.

measurement_evidence.description: Whether the cycle's two readings are in yet, in the same vocabulary cycle_sessions reports every session's evidence in. It computes nothing: the readings themselves are in cycle_sessions beside every other session, and whether the second is better than the first is the coach's judgment, never a score here. Null exactly when goal_context.measurement is null.

comparison_session_id.description: The session scheduled to repeat the reference, or null when nothing has been. Scheduling it is the coach's job at the review that rolls into the measurement week, not the athlete's to remember.

comparison_result.description: The same, plus scheduled for a session whose day has not passed and not_scheduled when nothing repeats the reference at all.

body_measurements.description: What the athlete says they weighed, day by day, or null when they have reported none. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates. Raw readings only: no trend, no rate of change, no comparison against a target — what a kilogram means inside this block is the coach's reading, and a direction computed here would have made that reading first. A day may carry either figure alone.

reported_activities.description: Sessions the athlete says they trained that no device recorded, from review_frame.detail_horizon_start onward, or null when they have reported none. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates. Beside recent_actuals, never inside it: these rows carry no activity id, no match confidence and no completion, so one can never be attached to a planned session or counted as a provider-backed actual. The athlete's word is evidence; it is simply not the provider's. A bulk import of months of training lands a row on every training day, and past the horizon those rows are training_history's monthly buckets rather than this list.

subjective_states.description: What the athlete said about how they felt, day by day over the last two weeks, in their own words — or null when they have said nothing, which is the ordinary starting state. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates. Stored as the sentence and never as a figure: a subjective feeling translated into a number is exactly what recovery_signals refuses, and this is the sentence that ban was protecting. Nothing deterministic reads these rows — no score, no run length, no comparison against the recovery readings beside them. "This is the third week of it" is the reading with the most value in it and it is the coach's to make. NOT the symptom channel: pain, illness, chest pain, dizziness and unusual symptoms belong in constraints.red_flags, where an explicit true limits the day deterministically rather than waiting to be read.

recovery_signals.description: Typed per-day recovery evidence for this turn, or null when no local reader or client upload supplied it. A client-uploaded group is labelled client-uploaded:<declared source>; that provenance says the hosted gateway validated and carried values supplied by the authenticated client, not that the gateway or Intervals observed them directly. Missing days and null values remain unknown. Nothing here is a readiness score invented by this product, a threshold, or an automatic training decision.

long_term_goals.description: What the athlete is training for beyond this cycle — a weight, a VO2max, a 5K time, a lift — or null when they have stated none, which is the ordinary starting state and the one to ask about. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates. Athlete-owned and cross-cycle: goal_context above is THIS cycle's milestone, which the coach chooses as one step toward these, and is never a second copy of them. The coach does not silently rewrite one; a target that no longer fits is raised with the athlete.

training_preferences.description: How the athlete says they like to train — Friday quality runs, five strength sessions, chest-back-legs — or null when they have stated none. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates. A starting point the coach may depart from with a reason, never a constraint: no validator reads these, and nothing here compares one against recent_actuals or cycle_sessions. A divergence between a stated habit and what was actually trained is visible from evidence already in this context and is the coach's to raise — the athlete owns whether the habit itself changes, and nothing infers that it lapsed. A pattern read out of history is not here and never becomes one: only what the athlete stated is.

training_history.description: The athlete's complete, unwindowed evidence history — spoken and imported activity summaries plus strength reports — rolled up into monthly buckets, or null when nothing long-range has been reported yet. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates. Answers what six weeks of recent_actuals structurally cannot: how a sport's volume has moved over months or a year, and how a movement's load has moved over its whole reported history. A coarse rollup and shaped to stay one — no activity_id, no match_confidence, no per-session row — so it can never be misread as recent_actuals's per-session truth (issue #101).

evidence_expectations.description: Which streams of dated evidence this athlete has ever produced, and when each one last did, or null when none ever has. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates. It exists because a stream that supplied evidence for months and then stopped currently looks exactly like one that was never there: both are a null group with an unknowns line that read the same on the first day it was ever built. A row is dates and counts only — no status, no expectation, no severity, no score — and nothing deterministic reads it (issue #28).

last_observed.description: The last date inside the window this signal carried a real (non-null, non-zero) value, or null when it carried none -- an acquisition fact, not a verdict on whether it is recent enough. Optional so a context built before the field existed still validates.

display_name.description: The athlete's own word for the lift, beside the canonical exercise key. An alias for anchoring: a report or prescription said in this word resolves to this entry.

adaptation.description: Null when the builder classified nothing: running is read against the athlete's own threshold and strength against what the session is, and a cross-training actual states sport, duration and heart rate without borrowing running's intensity bands.

body_stress.description: Null wherever the builder read no region from the record, which on a strength actual is always: the product does not map an activity to a body part, so which region was worked is in the athlete's own session_label and in the movements they report instead.

cost.description: Null wherever the builder derived no cost, which on a strength actual is always: the product does not judge what a lift cost from the activity record, so read its duration, heart rate, the athlete's stated feel and the recovery signals beside it instead.

completion.description: Occurrence status for reconciliation, not a reading of the prescription: 'completed' says this activity happened and is available to attach to a planned session, never that its prescribed steps or targets were met. A provider row carries it by virtue of the activity existing. Whether the prescription was met is read from the measurements beside it, and a claim about individual work steps only from evidence that can be associated with a prescribed step.

recorded_indoors.description: What the recording device said about where this run happened, from the provider's own flag rather than from the activity type -- a treadmill run is not always typed as one. true is a run recorded indoors, whose distance_km is the machine's reading rather than a measurement, so average_pace_sec_per_km is derived from that reading; false is a run the provider reported as not indoors; null is a run it said nothing about, and null on any sport other than running, where the flag is read for nothing. No correction is applied to any figure either way.

actual.description: One provider activity. Two shapes, one identity: a row whose settled (matched or owned) attachment put its reading on a cycle_sessions record carries only the required reconciliation fields plus paired_event_id -- read that record's activity for its measurements. Every other row -- today's session, an unmatched or probable activity, a pre-cycle one -- carries every field, because the context holds its reading nowhere else.

cycle_session.description: One session this cycle prescribed whose day has passed, rebuilt from the commit chain, with whatever came back for it beside the prescription. Rest days are not in it. A record for the coach to read: no completion percentage, and no status derived from a ratio. 'Planned but not done' is this record read for an absent activity; 'started but unfinished' is the same row read against the prescription. Per-set strength truth is not copied here — it stays in strength_execution, joined by date. A row from before the previous week may omit the attached activity's id; session_id still names the session, and every row carries what it prescribed.

week_start.description: The Monday of the natural week this session was scheduled in, so a cycle groups into the weeks the athlete trained rather than into seven-day slices counted back from today.

match_status.description: The PlanState value verbatim, from the last version that carried this session. 'completed' records that a trained session was matched or confirmed against this one, not that the prescription was met: adherence and execution quality are separate evidence, read from the activity beside it. 'partial' is a coaching judgment about what happened, never a value derived from a duration ratio.

prescription.description: What this session asked for, as garmin_coach_loop.prescription rendered it -- the same sentence the athlete reads. On every row, however old the week is: it is the planned half of planned-versus-actual, and a row without it says only its duration and cost, which does not distinguish an interval session from a tempo run. It states what was asked, never what was done: an attached activity is the other half, and whether the two agree is the coach's reading.

activity_evidence.description: Why the activity is what it is. Only 'none_found' -- this build read that day and nothing of that sport attached -- is evidence about the athlete. 'other_activity_same_day' means that sport was trained that day but attached to another session or to none, a matching question and not a missed session. 'athlete_reported' means no device recorded it and the athlete says they trained it, which is training: the watch being off or failing to sync is the ordinary reason a session is missing. It does not say the prescription was completed. 'outside_evidence_window' means the day is older than anything this build read.

cycle_session_activity.description: The activity deterministic matching attached to this session -- its whole reading, not a pointer: for a settled attachment the matching recent_actuals row is reduced to its reconciliation identity, so a measurement absent here is absent from the context. distance_km, average_pace_sec_per_km, elevation_gain_m and session_label appear by applicability -- distance, pace and elevation are not things a strength session has, and a session label is the provider's name for a strength session -- unless a value was measured anyway. activity_id appears on current- and previous-week rows only. match_confidence carries how firm the attachment is; 'probable' is a same-day, same-sport candidate, not a completion.

average_pace_sec_per_km.description: Averaged across the whole activity, warm-up and recoveries included. On a session that prescribed structure it is not a reading of the work; segment_execution is.

average_hr.description: Averaged across the whole activity, warm-up and recoveries included. On a session that prescribed structure it is not a reading of the work; segment_execution is.

subjective_feel.description: The athlete's own 1-5 feel for the session, when the provider carries one.

session_label.description: The athlete's own name for a strength session, straight from the provider.

recorded_indoors.description: What the recording device said about where this run happened, carried from the activity's own row. Once the match is settled this record is the reading -- the recent_actuals row beside it is reduced to its reconciliation identity -- so this is the only place left saying whether average_pace_sec_per_km came from a treadmill's distance or from a measured one. true is indoors, false is a run the provider reported as not indoors, null is one it said nothing about, and the key is absent on a sport the flag is not read for. No correction is applied.

source.description: athlete_reported. Stated on every row, not only on the group, so a row read on its own still says whose account of it this is.

reported_activity.description: One session the athlete reported. The absent keys are the contract: no activity_id, no match_confidence, no planned_session_id, no completion — there is nowhere for an attachment to be read out of.

provider_actual_same_day.description: True when recent_actuals also holds at least one activity of this sport on this date — the late-sync case where one session would otherwise stand in the context twice, once as the athlete's word and once as a provider actual. An observation only: whether the two are one session is the coach's reading, and nothing is merged or suppressed. False means checked and none found, never unchecked.

subjective_feel.description: The athlete's own 1-5 effort rating, the same scale recent_actuals carries, or null when they did not give one.

source.description: athlete_reported for a session the athlete described, athlete_imported for one read out of a file they uploaded. Both are the athlete's own evidence and neither is a provider-backed actual.

imported_from.description: Which upload supplied this session, when one did — the athlete's own name for the file, or the format it was read as. Null for a session the athlete described in conversation, which is what source also says. Neither kind is a provider actual: an upload is still the athlete handing over their own record of a session, and nothing here was observed by this product.

recovery_signals_day.description: One day's recovery readings, exactly as a device or app stated them. This is the stored shape, where a key that has always existed is written even when its value is null; the upload shape a client sends requires only date, and the gateway fills the readings it did not send with null on the way in. The five fields outside required arrived later than the others, so a context written before they existed omits them rather than carrying nulls for them.

sleep_score.description: Last night's sleep score, 0-100, as the device stated it.

sleep_duration_sec.description: Total sleep last night, in seconds.

sleep_history_score.description: Recent sleep trend across several nights, 0-100 -- not last night's own score.

hrv_last_night_ms.description: Last night's average HRV in milliseconds -- the single night beside hrv_7d_avg_ms's seven-day average.

resting_hr_bpm.description: Resting heart rate in beats per minute.

segment_execution.description: Per-segment execution for the recent runs the plan prescribed more than one step on, exactly as the provider grouped them. A run planned as one continuous effort is not here and is not missing: its average pace and average heart rate in recent_actuals report it completely, and its auto-laps report nothing further. Segments are not aligned to the session's prescribed steps: a prescribed warm-up plus five reps plus a cool-down can come back as fifteen segments with the warm-up split across two, so which segments are the work is a reading of the numbers and belongs to the coach. Null when no source could produce it.

recorded_indoors.description: What the recording device said about where this run happened, from the provider's own flag rather than from the activity type -- a treadmill run is not always typed as one. true is a run recorded indoors, whose distance is the machine's reading rather than a measurement, so every pace below is derived from that reading; false is a run the provider reported as not indoors; null is a run it said nothing about. No correction is applied to any figure either way.

index.description: Position in the provider's own ordering, so a coach can refer to a segment without renumbering it.

provider_type.description: What the provider called this segment. Not a claim that a WORK segment is the prescribed work -- on a real interval session almost every segment comes back typed WORK.

movement_history.description: Strength evidence grouped by movement, with what was prescribed on the same date beside it. The same figures strength_execution carries, pivoted from 'what was lifted that day' to 'how has this movement been going' -- the question a next prescription turns on. Carries no verdict: no completion rate, no progression score, no direction flag. Null when no strength evidence resolved to a movement.

exercise.description: The movement's grouping identity: the anchoring baseline entry's own key when one matches by key or display_name, else the reported spelling. Storage keeps the athlete's raw word; this merge happens at read time only.

display_name.description: The athlete's own word for the movement, from the baseline entry that anchors it. Null rather than the canonical key, which is an internal handle.

movement_history_occurrence.description: One session of this movement. Its raw sets and the athlete's notes live once, in strength_execution: this row's date plus its stored spelling (reported_as when present, the group's exercise otherwise) names the session that holds them. What rides here is the per-load arithmetic and the row's provenance, beside what was prescribed.

prescribed.description: Null means no plan prescribed this movement on this date -- trained off-plan, or older than the plan record. A list because one day can prescribe the same movement in parts.

reported_as.description: The raw spelling this row was stored under, present only when it differs from the group's merged name. Storage is keyed on the raw spelling, so a correction or retraction of this row must use this name.

movement_history_load_rollup.description: The arithmetic the session's own sets already answer, derived from strength_execution's array for this date and movement and never stored independently of it: reps at each distinct load, the session's total reps, and which load was heaviest and whether every set held it. No verdict of any kind -- see movement_history's own description.

total_reps.description: Null when any performed set in this occurrence has no recorded rep count -- a partial sum presented as complete would read a missing rep count as zero.

top_load.description: Null only when no set in the occurrence carries a measured weight_kg or assist_kg.

reps.description: Null when any set grouped into this load has no recorded rep count.

training_history.description: The athlete's complete, unwindowed evidence history rolled up into monthly buckets (issue #101). No verdict of any kind — no trend, no percentage change, no direction flag — matching movement_history's own stance one level up: two numbers and their months are the coaching evidence, and which way they point is the coach's reading.

source.description: Which provenances the kept months actually carry, joined with "+" in a fixed order (athlete_reported, athlete_imported, prescribed_confirmed) — the same style strength_execution's own source field uses one level up.

truncated.description: True when populated calendar months exist beyond the kept months array — it was cut to the most recent months, never silently dropped without saying so.

earliest_observed_month.description: The earliest calendar month (YYYY-MM) holding any evidence at all across the athlete's complete history, whether or not that month survived truncation. Always a real month: the group itself is null rather than present-but-empty when there is nothing to report.

movement_longevity.description: Each movement's earliest and heaviest observation, most recently observed movement first. Capped independently of months — an exercise vocabulary has no calendar to bound it — so a movement dropped for this cap can still be read inside a kept month bucket, just not broken out by name.

movement_longevity_truncated.description: True when more movements were observed than movement_longevity shows — cut to the most recently observed ones, never silently dropped without saying so. Same semantics as truncated above, scoped to movements instead of months.

training_history_month.description: One calendar month's evidence for one sport. Shaped to stay a rollup, never an actual: no activity_id, no per-session rows — session_count, not a list of sessions.

session_count.description: Every other sport counts reported/imported rows, one row per session by construction. Strength is the one exception: it counts distinct training days across both the coarse activity summary and the per-exercise strength report, because one gym visit can be described in both containers and must not be counted twice.

total_minutes.description: Sum of duration_minutes over rows in this bucket that stated one. Null — never zero — when none did, which is the ordinary case for a strength bucket built only from per-exercise reports; that source carries no duration field at all.

total_km.description: Sum of distance_km over rows in this bucket that stated one. Null — never zero — when none did. A partial, honestly-scoped total, not a claim that every session in the bucket carried a distance.

training_history_provenance_counts.description: How many of this bucket's rows carry each provenance. Fixed keys rather than a sparse map, always present at zero or above, so a reader never has to ask whether an absent key means zero or means the field does not exist here.

training_history_movement.description: One movement's earliest and heaviest observation across the athlete's complete, unwindowed strength-report history.

exercise.description: Same grouping identity as movement_history: the anchoring baseline entry's key when one matches, else the reported spelling.

display_name.description: The athlete's own word for the movement, from the baseline entry that anchors it. Null rather than the canonical key, which is an internal handle.

earliest.description: The first dated report of this movement on record. Never null: the movement's own key existing already means at least one dated report does.

heaviest.description: Null only when no occurrence of this movement ever carried a measured weight or assist figure at all — a bodyweight movement with nothing to compare.

training_history_observation.description: One dated load reading, reusing movement_history's own top_load shape: weighted beats assisted outright, and among assisted readings less assistance is the heavier direction.

held_every_set.description: False on a day with no measured weight or assistance at all — there was no load to hold, so true would assert a load-consistency question that never arose.

reported_as.description: Same contract as movement_history's occurrence field of this name.

evidence_expectations.description: One row per stream that has ever produced a dated observation (issue #28). A stream that never produced one has NO row, which is the whole false-positive control and is structural rather than a rule: never seen is not expected, and not expected is not reported, so an athlete who never claimed a recovery device is never told one is missing.

evidence_expectation_stream.description: One stream's supply record: when it first arrived, when it last did, how many observations there were, and how long the silence since has run. Dates and counts, and there is deliberately nowhere on this row to put a status, an expected flag, a severity, a score or a boolean for broken — what a gap means is the coach's reading, and a verdict computed here would be that reading made in the wrong layer.

stream.description: A fixed vocabulary, not an open string: at most one row per name, so the group is bounded by what this product can read rather than by how much the athlete trains. Both athlete-written streams count SPOKEN records only — athlete_reported_activities the sessions the athlete described, athlete_body_measurements the weigh-ins they stated. An upload is one event, so letting a file of a year's training or a year's weights set these dates would report a supply that ran for a year and stopped when somebody simply sent a file once. An upload's own rows are read by training_history instead.

basis.description: Which kind of evidence this row rests on. stored_record is a file this product keeps, so first_observed is the first day on record, full stop. read_window is a span this build asked a provider about, so first_observed is bounded by window_start beside it and says nothing about what came before.

window_start.description: The first day the read covered. Present on a read_window row and only there — on a stored_record row there is no window bounding anything, and a date here would claim one.

first_observed.description: The earliest day this stream produced an observation. The axis is the day the evidence is ABOUT, never the day it was recorded: a provider row carries no recording time at all, so the two kinds of stream would be measured on different clocks, and a bulk import of a year of training would collapse this onto its upload day.

last_observed.description: The most recent day this stream produced an observation. Never earlier than first_observed.

observations.description: How many dated observations the stream produced, counting rows rather than distinct days — two lifts logged on one day are two observations of a stream that is producing. At least one: a row exists because the stream produced something.

days_since_last.description: Days from last_observed to the context's as_of. Zero on the day it last produced. It is the length of a silence in the record and nothing more — it is not graded, not compared against a threshold, and does not mean the athlete stopped training. freshness answers how this turn's read went; this answers what the record holds, and the two are different questions.

baseline_evidence_threshold_pace_row.description: The fastest whole-run average pace observed, with the run's distance beside it. A whole-run average spans warm-up and recoveries; the label is what keeps it from reading as a threshold measurement.

baseline_evidence_max_hr_row.description: The highest whole-activity average heart rate observed, any sport. An average bounds a maximum from below; it never measures one.

baseline_evidence_easy_hr_row.description: The range of average heart rates across runs this context already classified easy. The range is reported, not the excess over the ceiling.

baseline_evidence_weekly_volume_row.description: Observed running per natural Monday-to-Sunday week, newest first, only weeks the evidence window holds in full. Zero runs is a statement about this window of the feed, not a claim the athlete trained nothing.

through.description: The last date this week's tally includes. Before the week's Sunday it states the week is still open; km null means a run in the week carries no recorded distance, so the total is unknown rather than zero.

baseline_evidence_strength_row.description: One strength movement's written baseline beside the loads it was actually worked at -- movement_history's occurrences grouped once more, by the day's top working weight (or least assistance, the heavier direction for an assisted lift).

exercise.description: Same grouping identity as movement_history: the anchoring baseline entry's key when one matches, else the reported spelling.

metric.description: What is being aimed at, in the athlete's own words — body weight, VO2max, a 5K time, a lift. Also the identity a restatement lands on.

target.description: Where they want it, exactly as stated and never converted: "50", "80 kg", "sub-25:00". Not a current value — there is deliberately no field for one, because the provider and the athlete's own reported measurements already hold that and a third copy would be a parallel truth.

target_date.description: By when, or null when they named no date. A date already past is kept rather than refused: a goal that came due unmet is a real state, and one worth raising.

note.description: Anything else the athlete said about this goal, or null.

recorded_at.description: When they stated it. Age is context, never expiry — a goal does not lapse by going unmentioned.

date.description: The day the athlete's statement is about, which is not always the day they made it — "昨天很累" is an ordinary thing to say a day late.

note.description: What they said, verbatim and untranslated. Free text and unparsed on purpose: the moment this is machine-readable something starts computing with it, and a computed reading of how somebody feels is the thing this field exists instead of.

recorded_at.description: When they said it. Age is context the coach weighs, never expiry: a statement does not stop having been made.

topic.description: What the habit is about, and the identity a later restatement lands on.

statement.description: The habit, in the athlete's own words. Free text and unparsed — a machine-readable habit is one something starts checking plans against, and a preference that can fail a plan has become a constraint.

recorded_at.description: When the athlete stated it. Only they change or drop it: a habit is not inferred to have lapsed from their having stopped doing it.

run_drift_end.description: One end of a run, averaged over that third of its samples. A series the device never recorded is absent from both ends rather than filled in; each series is thirded on its own samples, so one missing series costs the others nothing. average_cadence_spm is the provider's own figure and counts one leg: the number a runner or a watch calls cadence is twice it. Cadence is the only value here an athlete can act on during a run -- ground contact time is what a fade did, not something to instruct. Step length is not carried because pace and cadence already state it: speed is cadence times step length.

run_drift_activity.description: One run's first third against its last third.

run_drift.description: Heart rate, pace, step length and ground contact time at each end of the recent runs, so a session that cost more than it produced is visible at all: an average cannot separate a run held steady from one that drifted. Reports the two ends and nothing else -- whether a rise is heat, fatigue, or terrain is the coach's reading. Runs shorter than fifteen minutes are not here, because thirds of them differ by warm-up. At most the six most recent runs in the window are read, and a run left unread is named in unknowns. Null when no source could produce it.

set_structure_activity.description: One strength session's shape in time, read out of the file the watch uploaded. No exercise, no reps and no load: the device's exercise field is a list of its own guesses, its rep counts disagree with what the athlete logged, and weight is absent unless typed in on the watch. Those three come from the athlete through strength_execution.

set_structure.description: Working-set count, time under load, and rest and set length at each end of the recent strength sessions. The provider parses none of this -- it stores the watch's file and reports only duration, heart rate and load -- so this is the only view of what happened inside a strength session that does not depend on the athlete recounting it. Two sessions of equal duration and load can run opposite ways here. At most the six most recent sessions in the window are read, and a session left unread is named in unknowns. Null when no source could produce it.
